name: Mystique
bio: Shapeshifter and leader of the Brotherhood; mother of Nightcrawler, foster mother of Rogue, lifelong partner of Destiny. Her relationships are the franchise's clearest study in how a villain can love people and still fail them.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: 90s / Blue-Gold
era.description: Jim Lee's X-Men relaunch through the Onslaught and Apocalypse: The Twelve era. Rogue and Gambit, the Blue and Gold teams, Age of Apocalypse.

relationships.label: Mother who abandoned him
relationships.summary: Hinted at since Uncanny X-Men #142 (1981) and confirmed in 1994: Mystique bore Kurt and, fleeing a mob, let him fall into a river. The relationship is about whether he can forgive her and whether she wants him to. Krakoa, where she sat on the Quiet Council while he served as its moral voice, kept the question open.

events.note: Mystique hints she knows Nightcrawler's parentage.
Mystique confirms she is Kurt's mother.
'The Draco' names Azazel as his father.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Foster mother and daughter
relationships.summary: Mystique and Destiny raised Rogue after her powers manifested, then used her as a Brotherhood weapon. Rogue's defection to the X-Men was a betrayal from Mystique's side and an escape from Rogue's; the two have spent decades alternating between manipulation and genuine care.

events.note: Rogue debuts as Mystique's protégé, absorbing Ms. Marvel's powers permanently.
Rogue asks Xavier for help and joins the X-Men.
Rogue gains control of her power; Mystique's manipulations in the surrounding arc resurface.

continuity.name: Earth-616

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Lifelong partners
relationships.summary: Claremont wrote them as a couple from Destiny's first appearance, in code, because editorial would not allow it to be stated. Destiny's death in Uncanny X-Men #255 (1990) drove Mystique's choices for decades; her Krakoan resurrection, which Mystique forced, is the spine of Inferno (2021) and Immortal X-Men.

events.note: Destiny debuts with the Brotherhood alongside Mystique.
Destiny is resurrected; the two are stated on the page as married.
